source_candidate.claim_family: Share public strict-NLU artifact lifecycle versus paper-level retained task coefficients

primary_sources.title: Shared LoRA Subspaces for almost Strict Continual Learning
verified_points: Method explicitly retains one shared basis plus t task-specific coefficient sets after merging.
Eq. 3/4 and surrounding text recalculate coefficients for all prior tasks i<=t.
Continual GLUE table reports Share/Share-full active parameter footprint 0.012M and 0.29MB.

mechanical_findings.finding: The pinned strict-NLU training loop carries exactly the immediately previous trained EigenFlux path forward as the next task's load_path; after training, prev_adapter_path is replaced by the current task's save_path.

Each run_glue invocation constructs an EigenFlux adapter under the current task/evaluation adapter name and loads the supplied artifact into that same adapter name. PeftModel.load_adapter only creates a new adapter if that name is absent; because get_peft_model already created the named adapter, loading the predecessor artifact populates the current adapter rather than preserving a separate historical adapter entry.

evaluate_previous_tasks passes the same current adapter_path to every prior GLUE task. The eval task name chooses dataset/head semantics and the in-process adapter namespace, but there is no search/selection over a bank of historical coefficient artifacts in this main path.
mechanical_findings.scope: Pinned strict-NLU driver only; this does not rule out other repository modalities or unpublished experiment code.

mechanical_findings.finding: The EigenFlux saver emits components/loadings for the adapter state and strips the adapter-name suffix for serialization. In this strict-NLU invocation there is one carried adapter state, so the current saved continuation artifact is a current shared-state snapshot, not an embedded t-way historical coefficient bank.
mechanical_findings.scope: Pinned peft save/load implementation as exercised by the strict-NLU driver.

mechanical_findings.finding: update_previous_weights is post-hoc and only updates the immediately previous task using previous+current reconstructions, saving a standalone <prev>_updated.safetensors. The main loop does not assign that updated file to prev_adapter_path, so it is not the continuation state for the next task; it is an archival/evaluation side output.

verdict.summary: The sealed worker correction is supported and can be strengthened: at this pinned commit the public strict-NLU driver is operationally a single evolving EigenFlux snapshot with task-known evaluation, not an inference router over retained historical coefficient sets. The paper, by contrast, explicitly defines and counts t lightweight coefficient sets and gives storage O(k(d+m)+Tkp). Therefore the paper's method-level storage/accounting contract and the public strict-NLU driver's carried state are not the same object.
important_scope_corrections: Do not call the strict public NLU driver an oracle selector over historical Share coefficient sets; the main evaluation path does not expose such a bank.

Do not interpret the paper's 0.29MB active Share figure as the size of the entire retained public experiment output tree. The script separately saves one trained directory per task plus post-hoc updated prior-task files, so retained experiment/archive storage grows with task count even though the carried continuation state is one current artifact.

Do not infer that the Share method itself lacks t coefficient sets. The paper explicitly defines them; this audit identifies a paper-versus-public-NLU-driver contract distinction, not a falsification of the paper's abstract method.
Do not generalize this result to Diffusion, NLG, unpublished code, or another commit without separate inspection.

next_verification: Quantify SLoRA's per-task archival state and reconstruction cost at pinned alina1031/SLoRA@0faf15fd6562ed3e146e8733205f59ef9742ba0f, and determine whether the public scripts support a lossless compacted merged checkpoint that removes the need to retain/replay all prior per-task denoised deltas.
